      "body": "`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is suppressed for TL0 users when anonymous viewers are restricted, but the new derived attribute `website_name` is not. Since `website_name` exposes the host/path of the same user-supplied website, anonymous users can see the website URL (or parts of it) via `website_name` even when `website` itself is hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or apply the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?` check."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/serializers/user_serializer.rb",
      "line": 153,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "include_website_name is missing the question mark expected by the serializer",
      "body": "Discourse/ActiveModel::Serializer inclusion gates use `include_<attribute>?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). The method is named `include_website_name`, so it will not be called to decide whether `website_name` should be serialized. The intended `website.present?` condition is therefore ineffective, and the field may be serialized even when blank or invalid. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or rely on `untrusted_attributes` for the inclusion logic."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/serializers/user_serializer.rb",
      "line": 149,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Same-domain check misses website subdomains of the Discourse host",
      "body": "The logic appends the path when the hosts are equal, when both have the same label count and share a suffix, or when the Discourse host is a subdomain of the website host. It does not handle the common reverse case where Discourse is on the apex domain and the user's website is a subdomain, e.g. Discourse `example.com` and website `http://www.example.com/user`. In that case `discourse_host.ends_with?(\".www.example.com\")` is false, so only the host is shown even though it is the same site. The comparison needs to handle this direction too, ideally using registrable-domain logic."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/serializers/user_serializer.rb",
      "line": 144,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Domain comparison is naive and can match unrelated public-suffix domains",
      "body": "The host comparison treats hosts as equivalent if they share the suffix after removing the first label. This can falsely match unrelated hosts on public suffixes, such as `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` or `www.gov.uk` vs `forum.gov.uk`, causing the serializer to display the full path for websites that are not actually on the same registered domain as the instance. A proper eTLD+1/registrable-domain comparison would avoid these false positives."
    },
    {
      "file": "spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb",
      "line": 11,
      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Untrusted attribute spec does not cover website_name",
      "body": "The spec asserting that TL0 users seen by anonymous do not serialize untrusted attributes lists `website` but omits the new `website_name`. Because `website_name` exposes the same user-supplied website information, it should be included in this list once the serializer treats it as untrusted. Without this coverage, the current leakage of `website_name` for restricted users is not detected."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6",
      "line": 210,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "website_name is not refreshed after saving a changed website",
      "body": "The profile template now displays the server-generated `model.website_name` instead of computing it from `model.website` on the client. However `User.save` only updates `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response and does not update `website_name` or merge the returned user payload. If a user changes their website in preferences, the locally cached `website_name` can remain stale or nil until the user model is reloaded, whereas the previous client-side computed `websiteName` would have tracked `model.website`. Update the model from the server response or recompute the display client-side."

findings.title: website_name is not hidden by the untrusted-attribute rules
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is suppressed for TL0 users when anonymous viewers are restricted, but the new derived attribute `website_name` is not. Since `website_name` exposes the host/path of the same user-supplied website, anonymous users can see the website URL (or parts of it) via `website_name` even when `website` itself is hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or apply the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?` check.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the question mark expected by the serializer
findings.body: Discourse/ActiveModel::Serializer inclusion gates use `include_<attribute>?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). The method is named `include_website_name`, so it will not be called to decide whether `website_name` should be serialized. The intended `website.present?` condition is therefore ineffective, and the field may be serialized even when blank or invalid. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or rely on `untrusted_attributes` for the inclusion logic.

findings.title: Same-domain check misses website subdomains of the Discourse host
findings.body: The logic appends the path when the hosts are equal, when both have the same label count and share a suffix, or when the Discourse host is a subdomain of the website host. It does not handle the common reverse case where Discourse is on the apex domain and the user's website is a subdomain, e.g. Discourse `example.com` and website `http://www.example.com/user`. In that case `discourse_host.ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so only the host is shown even though it is the same site. The comparison needs to handle this direction too, ideally using registrable-domain logic.

findings.title: Domain comparison is naive and can match unrelated public-suffix domains
findings.body: The host comparison treats hosts as equivalent if they share the suffix after removing the first label. This can falsely match unrelated hosts on public suffixes, such as `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` or `www.gov.uk` vs `forum.gov.uk`, causing the serializer to display the full path for websites that are not actually on the same registered domain as the instance. A proper eTLD+1/registrable-domain comparison would avoid these false positives.

findings.title: Untrusted attribute spec does not cover website_name
findings.body: The spec asserting that TL0 users seen by anonymous do not serialize untrusted attributes lists `website` but omits the new `website_name`. Because `website_name` exposes the same user-supplied website information, it should be included in this list once the serializer treats it as untrusted. Without this coverage, the current leakage of `website_name` for restricted users is not detected.

findings.title: website_name is not refreshed after saving a changed website
findings.body: The profile template now displays the server-generated `model.website_name` instead of computing it from `model.website` on the client. However `User.save` only updates `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response and does not update `website_name` or merge the returned user payload. If a user changes their website in preferences, the locally cached `website_name` can remain stale or nil until the user model is reloaded, whereas the previous client-side computed `websiteName` would have tracked `model.website`. Update the model from the server response or recompute the display client-side.
